heading: Explaining capital across countries
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 3 with a precomputed slider for the depreciation rate
plot_title: Data and the Solow prediction with d = 0.07
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [Penn World Table 11.0](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/), Groningen Growth and Development Centre ([DOI 10.34894/FABVLR](https://doi.org/10.34894/FABVLR)), variables `csh_i` (investment share) and `rgdpo` (real GDP); cite as Feenstra, Inklaar and Timmer (2015), ["The Next Generation of the Penn World Table"](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20130954), *American Economic Review* 105(10). Capital is our own perpetual-inventory estimate from PWT investment, with 5 percent depreciation. The straight line is the Solow model's prediction, $K/Y = s/d$.
Prepared file: [`data/ch05/fig5-3.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch05/fig5-3.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch05/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 5.3 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

source_note:
